output.summary: The FY2026 revenue jump came from the commodity price rally. Bushels were flat (-0.9%), the auditor attributes the margin gain to inventory appreciation, and peers grew revenue 41% without any new program. The cooperative ranked 10th of 23 on net savings growth, so the Operational Excellence program is not shown to have caused the result. The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes entirely from maintenance cut by about a third while deferred work orders tripled. Harlan Junction has unresolved dust and monitoring hazards that the insurer wants fixed by 21 November, and the near-miss was closed without the required investigation. Drying and grading depend on one 63-year-old Superintendent with no successor. The expansion proposal rests on FY2026 prices and an unsourced throughput assumption, so its financial viability is unestablished. Fix the hazards, start succession, and rebuild the financial case before voting.
